title: Entries of a doubled bit string
statement: Let $w$ be a finite Boolean word, let $c$ be an index with $c<|w|$, and let $p$ be a Boolean. At position $2c+p$ (where $p$ is identified with $0$ or $1$), the doubled word has value $w_c$.
replaced:
Let $w = w_0 w_1 \cdots w_{n-1}$ be a bit string, let $c < n$, and let
$p \in \{0, 1\}$.  Then the doubling $\mathrm{dbl}(w)$ (each bit of $w$
written twice in succession, positions indexed from $0$) has a symbol at
position $2c + p$, and that symbol is $w_c$.
